boundary_condition: This is a qualitative airfare-shopping habit only; do not reuse any one quoted dollar amount as a standing budget ceiling, and do not apply it to destinations, dates, hotels, or other travel categories unless separately stated.
condition: When searching for flights and multiple options satisfy the trip-specific requirements, treat lower price or staying within the stated trip budget as an important selection factor.
default_action: Prefer cheaper or in-budget flight options before more expensive alternatives, and consider cost-saving tradeoffs such as economy cabin or an added stop when the user has not made those features non-negotiable.
exception_condition: If the cheapest fare violates a hard trip constraint the user states for the current request, do not select it solely because it is cheaper; instead surface the price-versus-constraint tradeoff and ask whether to relax the constraint.
name: Keeps flight costs low when possible
rationale: The cited conversations vary in their one-off amounts and constraints, but they consistently show cost sensitivity: some users give a maximum spend, others ask for cheap flights, and one is willing to add a stop for a cheaper fare. This supports a reusable qualitative default of budget-sensitive flight selection, not a reusable numeric cap.

source_evidence.contribution: The user says, “I don't want to spend anymore than $350,” supporting attention to a trip-specific budget limit.
The user asks for “The cheap is possible” and accepts economy, supporting a low-cost flight preference.
The user says they are “looking to spend up to $3,500,” showing another trip-specific price cap rather than a reusable numeric ceiling.
The user requests “a non-stop and a cheap flight,” grounding cheapness as an airfare selection criterion.
The user is willing to make one stop “if it would get me a cheaper flight,” supporting price-sensitive tradeoffs.

source_examples.user_utterance: I don't want to spend anymore than $350.
The cheap is possible, the economy is cool and gives me Wi-Fi.
Yes. I'd like a nonstop flight and that's pretty much it. And I'm looking to spend up well. I'm looking to spend up to $3,500.
Just a non-stop and a cheap flight.
I would prefer a non-stop flight, but I'm willing to compromise and make one stop if it would get me a cheaper flight.
